title: What holds a cell up, and what makes it climb

objectives.statement: Given a stated mechanical demand and the length over which it acts, predict which of the three cytoskeletal filament systems can meet it by comparing persistence length against that length, by testing whether the demand requires a direction, and by testing whether it requires survival under large deformation, and name the property that decided the case.

Place the four attachment structures of a colonic absorptive cell in apical-to-basal order, name the cytoskeletal polymer each one anchors and the proteins that make the link, and use that map to predict which functions survive and which fail when a named component is lost.

Weigh the evidence for and against proliferation in the crypt being the force that drives cells upward, state for each study what its design can and cannot establish about that force, and name the measurement that would discriminate between the competing accounts.

scenes.title: A finger of fluid, standing up
Three polymers, and what each one's stiffness will let it do
Choosing a polymer for a stated job
Four attachments, and which polymer each one grips
What moves a cell up a crypt
Practice: decide, then defend the decision
Clinical wrap-up: which attachment does a leak implicate?
